newhire_ryan: Morning all, I'm ryan, starting today! Running into a couple of weird dev env issues on my M1 Mac: installed Homebrew and asdf per the onboarding, but running `node` or `python` gives me different versions than expected (system python shows up). Also pipx-installed CLIs aren't on PATH. My dotfiles are a mix from previous jobs. Any quick recommended minimal dotfile snippets or PATH ordering we use here? Do we prefer brew-managed tools or asdf-first?

emma: welcome ryan! We standardize on asdf for language runtimes to avoid brew/python collisions. Minimal zsh additions we recommend in `~/.zprofile`:
```bash
# Homebrew for Apple Silicon
export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$PATH
# initialize asdf (installed via brew)
. "$(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh" || true
# ensure user-local bin (pipx etc) is after asdf python but before system
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```
That usually puts asdf-managed python/node first.

devx_noah: +1. For pipx, install into the asdf python env: `python -m pip install --user pipx && pipx ensurepath`. Then open a new shell. If you previously had pipx from brew, `brew remove pipx` to avoid two pipx installs.

infra-bot: See onboarding snippet at <internal/dev-setup/env-boot.md> for zsh/bash/fish examples. Also remember `~/.zprofile` runs for login shells on macOS and `~/.zshrc` for interactive. Put PATH and asdf init in zprofile.

sarah: small gotcha: if you have pyenv or rbenv leftover, check `which -a python` and `which -a node` to see all candidates. Remove or uninstall old ones to avoid surprises. I usually remove pyenv: `brew uninstall pyenv && rm -rf ~/.pyenv` if you're switching to asdf.

newhire_ryan: thanks! quick follow-up: what about VS Code terminal vs GUI apps? I noticed Terminal.app shows correct PATH but apps launched from Finder don't.

emma: yep that's macOS login environment stuff. If you launch VS Code from Dock it gets a different PATH. Easiest: start VS Code from terminal with `code .` once configured, or add the PATH lines to `~/.zprofile` (login shells). For GUI apps on Big Sur+ you can also `exec -l zsh` in `.zprofile` to ensure interactive behaviour, but `code .` is simplest.

devx_noah: also check `asdf reshim` after installing binaries so shims point to right executables. And `asdf current` shows which versions are active in the repo (check `.tool-versions`).

newhire_ryan: great — I ran `which -a python` and saw `/usr/bin/python3` then a brew path. After exporting PATH with /opt/homebrew first and sourcing asdf script it now shows asdf python. Pipx still missing but I'll reinstall into asdf python.

emma: perfect. If you want my starter dotfiles (company tweaks + a small zshrc) I can share a gist. We try to keep them minimal (no secrets). Ping me and I'll drop link.

newhire_ryan: would love that, thanks everyone! I'll post outputs if anything still acts up.
